narrative.overview:
An air-traffic controller works a rack of printed strips, one per flight, each in a coloured holder; a strip that needs something is pulled half out so it stands proud, and a flight that leaves the airspace has its strip removed. The board carries no totals and no history. That is this product's oldest rule wearing somebody else's uniform, so the whole app is built as one of those boards.

Every note, chore, task and appointment is a strip. The four rooms are four bays. Squirrel choosing one thing is a physical act rather than a highlight: one strip pulled out of its rack, with the rule that chose it printed on it. Answering something strikes it and drops it into the day's tray, and the tray is empty again tomorrow.

The two faces and the whole palette are pinned by the owner and survived the redesign unchanged. The card, the chip, the bubble, the dock, the lid and the 3px sticker outline did not.
keyCharacteristics: One unit: a strip is the only content object, at every size.
One grid: every band aligns to the same row rhythm, sentences included.
State is a mark, never a fill — a strip is struck and moved, never repainted.
Colour on a left edge is a holder, never an accent.
Exactly one strip is pulled, ever.
Nothing is drawn as speech; Buddy writes in the margin, in pencil.

rules.name: The Holder Rule
rules.body: The colour down a strip's left edge is the plastic sleeve the slip sits in, and must read as one: 11px, ruled off by the same 2px outline, carrying a grip mark. It says which bay the strip belongs to and nothing else — never a severity, never a state, never a category accent.

rules.name: The Four Holders
rules.body: notes purple, chores orange, tasks amber, agenda brown. Amber and brown are also state colours, and that is safe only because no state ever fills a strip. If a state becomes a fill, change the holders rather than the rule.

rules.name: The State Is A Mark Rule
rules.body: State is drawn by striking the words in pencil and by the strip's position — in the rack, or in the tray. Never a fill, never a coloured dot, never a badge. Twelve strips tinted twelve ways is a chart of how you are doing.

rules.name: Green Is Only Done
rules.body: state-done appears on the did-it stamp and as a mark in the tray. Never a holder, never furniture, never an accent.

rules.name: The Orange Ink Rule
rules.body: Ink on orange is the outline, never white or paper: white on #e66d0d measures 3.1:1, the mark's near-black 5.78:1. A contrast fact, carried unchanged from the previous world.

rules.name: The Lifted Fill Rule
rules.body: A state colour used as a stamp fill is raised toward white until the outline reads on it. The unlifted value is for marks and ink, never for a fill under type.

rules.name: The Focus Ring Rule
rules.body: orange-lit on the field, violet on stock, where orange-lit measures 2.03:1 against the 3:1 an indicator needs. Every surface taking card or paper is in the violet list; this goes wrong by omission.

rules.name: Never A White Surface
rules.body: Card stock is the tail's cream lightened. There is no white in the interface; a surface that reads as neutral has failed to be Squirrel.

rules.name: The Field Exception
rules.body: The ground keeps the lit radial at .35 alpha and the 22px dot grid: .5 put cream at 4.19:1 on the lit centre, .35 puts it at 4.8:1. The one gradient the product allows, and nothing pressable may take one.

rules.name: The Printed Figure Rule
rules.body: Times, dates and countdowns are Inter Black with tabular figures — on a board a number is a printed thing, not a sentence. The only content use of Inter in the product.

rules.name: Two Axes, One Face
rules.body: His words and Buddy's are casual; furniture is precise. A sign, stamp or mark in the casual axis reads as somebody speaking, which furniture must never do.

rules.name: The Step-Up Rule
rules.body: Below 620px the reading roles step up — strip to 15.5px, pulled to 21px — while furniture stays put.

rules.name: No All-Caps Sentences
rules.body: Caps are for signs, stamps and marks: three words, never a sentence. The rule that pulled a strip is sentence case with a small PULLED tag beside it.

rules.name: Depth Is Distance From The Rack
rules.body: The only thing a shadow may say is how far out of its holder a strip has been pulled. No hover elevation for its own sake, no floating panel, no modal on a scrim.

rules.name: Cocking Is The Only Selected State
rules.body: A strip with your attention lifts 3px out of the rack and stays there while it is being worked. This replaces every highlight, tint, badge and left-border the product might otherwise grow.

rules.name: The 1150ms Hold Is A Requirement
rules.body: An answered strip strikes, then stays put for 1150ms before travelling to the tray, because the undo has to live somewhere while you decide. Shortening it removes the undo's home.

rules.name: Nothing Fades
rules.body: A fade is what a screen does; a rack does not. The only opacity transition is the reduced-motion fallback.

dos: Do draw every content object as a strip, at every viewport.
Do put colour only where it means a bay, an action, or a state in the tray.
Do print the rule that pulled a strip on the strip.
Do keep the 1150ms hold before anything leaves the board.
Do let an empty rack look like an empty rack.
Do set times, dates and countdowns in Inter Black with tabular figures.
donts: Don't reintroduce a card, a chip, a bubble or a bottom composer.
Don't fill a strip with a state colour, or tint a row by category.
Don't pull more than one strip.
Don't give Buddy a face, a column, or more than one line on an object.
Don't put a number on a bay sign that counts what you did not do.
Don't use white anywhere, and don't let a surface read as neutral.
Don't add a hover elevation, a modal, or a floating panel.
